title: Regiment and Compass
premise: In the winter of 1918, Bram Montrose keeps the light at Gullwrack Point and raises his late wife's two siblings as his own. When a sealed letter washes ashore implicating their family in a coastal smuggling ring supplying a deserter network, Bram must decide whether to protect his fragile found family or surrender them to an army investigator who arrives with the storms. As the armistice negotiations stall and the workshop where the family repairs signal equipment becomes evidence, they race to finish one last beacon before it is seized. The letter's true author — Bram's dead wife, who foresaw the plot — is revealed, and the family chooses each other over blood, standing together when the investigator finally comes.
about_author: Lena Brightwater grew up in a lighthouse family on the North Sea coast and spent a decade restoring maritime archives before turning to fiction. Her novels explore how ordinary keepers of small lights survive the great storms of history.

chapters.title: The Weight of Glass
chapters.summary: Bram Montrose's POV. A routine storm season opens: Bram polishes lenses, mends nets, and quietly mothers his late wife's siblings, Wren and Tam, while keeping grief at arm's length through work. Emotional beat: tender loneliness disguised as competence; the family functions but never speaks of the woman who bound them.

chapters.title: What the Tide Brought
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. After the worst gale in memory, Wren finds a sealed oilskin packet wedged in the rocks bearing her sister's handwriting — dated three years after her death. Emotional beat: uncanny hope curdling into dread as the letter names the family and warns of a plot 'no one wants a part of.'

chapters.title: A Visitor with Clean Boots
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. Army investigator Captain Ellery Voss arrives, ostensibly inspecting coastal signals, asking pointed questions about shipments and deserters. Bram lies for the first time in his careful life. Emotional beat: the keeper's instinct to guard the light now turned inward, toward guarding people.

chapters.title: The Workshop Ledger
chapters.summary: Tam's POV. Tam discovers the family workshop has been used to repair smuggled signal gear — by someone with access to their tools and Bram's signature stamp. Emotional beat: betrayal and confusion; the boy who idolizes Bram must reconcile the man he trusts with the evidence before him.

chapters.title: Salt and Silence
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Wren decodes more of the letter: her sister infiltrated the smuggling ring to protect the family and left instructions hidden in the workshop walls. She tells no one. Emotional beat: the burden of inheritance — carrying a secret that could save or shatter them all.

chapters.title: The Armistice That Wouldn't Come
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. News spreads that peace talks have stalled; Voss's pressure intensifies, and a raid on the cove is imminent. Bram confronts Tam about the ledger, and the truth cracks the family open. Emotional beat: rage, then raw honesty — the first time they speak of the dead wife as a person, not a wound.

chapters.title: Instructions in the Wall
chapters.summary: Tam's POV. Following Wren's lead, the siblings open the wall cavity and find their sister's full confession and a plan: finish rebuilding the sabotaged harbor beacon so the rescue boats can navigate the next storm, proving the family's innocence through the work itself. Emotional beat: purpose replacing fear; found family forged into a crew.

chapters.title: Storm Warning
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Voss returns with warrants as the greatest storm of the year bears down. The workshop is sealed as evidence with half the beacon parts inside. Wren bargains with Voss using her sister's letters — proof the family was targeted, not guilty. Emotional beat: defiance born of love; the stakes made flesh.

chapters.title: The Light They Kept
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. Climax. In the teeth of the gale, the family breaks into their own sealed workshop, carries the lens through floodwater, and mounts the beacon as the armistice is signed at dawn — just as rescue boats need the light. Voss watches from the gallery, warrant in hand, and does not stop them. Emotional beat: triumph inseparable from sacrifice.

chapters.title: Regiment and Compass
chapters.summary: Tam's POV. Resolution. Voss closes the file; the sister's name is cleared posthumously. The family buries the letters beside her grave and relights the lamp for the first night of peace. Emotional beat: belonging fully chosen at last — not kept by duty or grief, but by decision, like a light deliberately lit.
